topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.241, must every Pennsylvania broker maintain a main office within the Commonwealth?
choice_a: Yes, unless the broker maintains a main office in another state where the broker holds the equivalent of a standard license
choice_b: No -- Pennsylvania brokers are never required to maintain any office, in-state or out-of-state
choice_c: Yes, with no exception, even if the broker is licensed and headquartered entirely in another state
choice_d: Only brokers who employ more than five salespersons must maintain a main office
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.241(a) requires a broker, cemetery broker, or rental listing referral agent to maintain a main office in Pennsylvania unless the licensee maintains a main office in another state where the licensee holds the equivalent of a standard license.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: How many routine inspections per year may the Real Estate Commission conduct of a broker's office under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.246, and what must occur before an inspection begins?
choice_a: No more than four routine inspections per year during regular business hours, and the Commission must inform the office manager that an inspection is occurring and explain its scope
choice_b: Unlimited routine inspections at any hour, with no advance notice of any kind
choice_c: Exactly one inspection per year, scheduled at least 30 days in advance by certified mail
choice_d: No more than four inspections per year, but only with a court-issued search warrant
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.246 caps routine Commission inspections at four per year during regular business hours (with additional special inspections permitted for complaints, reasonable suspicion of violations, or follow-up on prior noncompliance), and requires the Commission to inform the office manager that an inspection is occurring and explain its limited scope before beginning.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: During an office inspection under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.246, which of the following may Commission representatives do?
choice_a: Examine transaction records, inspect the premises, interview employees, and obtain the broker's written authorization to the bank where the escrow account is maintained
choice_b: Seize and permanently retain the broker's original transaction files without providing copies
choice_c: Only review records that the broker voluntarily chooses to produce, with no examination of the premises itself
choice_d: Interview clients of the brokerage directly, but not the brokerage's own employees
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.246 permits Commission representatives, during an inspection, to examine transaction records, inspect the office premises, interview employees, and obtain the broker's or cemetery broker's written authorization to the bank or depository where the escrow account is maintained.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Following revocation of a Pennsylvania real estate license, how long must an individual wait before the Commission will even consider relicensure, and is approval automatic once that time passes?
choice_a: At least 5 years, and even then relicensure is within the Commission's discretion, not automatic
choice_b: At least 1 year, after which relicensure is granted automatically upon request
choice_c: There is no waiting period, only a discretionary review
choice_d: At least 10 years, with automatic relicensure once that period expires
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.251 provides that the Commission will not authorize relicensure of an individual whose license was revoked for at least 5 years following the date revocation begins, and even after that period, the decision to permit relicensure remains within the Commission's discretion, requiring the individual to satisfy all current licensure requirements.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Within how many days of a sole-proprietor broker's death must the estate notify the Commission that it has appointed a licensed broker to oversee termination of the business, and what is that appointed broker barred from doing?
choice_a: 15 days; the appointed broker may not enter into any new listing agreements
choice_b: 30 days; the appointed broker may freely enter into new listing agreements
choice_c: 90 days; the appointed broker may not communicate with existing clients
choice_d: 60 days; the appointed broker may not close any pending transactions
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.252 requires the estate of a deceased sole-proprietor broker to notify the Commission within 15 days that it has appointed a licensed broker to oversee termination of the business, and bars that appointed broker from entering into new listing agreements.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.252, what happens to a deceased sole-proprietor broker's unexpired listing agreements, and may the appointed broker hire new licensees?
choice_a: Unexpired listings may continue to be promoted (unless the seller or lessor cancels) but automatically expire 90 days after the broker's death and cannot be renewed; no new licensees may be hired
choice_b: All unexpired listings terminate immediately upon death, and the appointed broker may hire new licensees freely
choice_c: Unexpired listings continue indefinitely with no expiration, and new licensees may be hired without restriction
choice_d: Unexpired listings may be renewed once for an additional term, and one new licensee may be hired to replace the deceased broker
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.252 allows unexpired listing agreements to continue being promoted unless the seller or lessor elects to cancel, but they automatically expire 90 days after the broker's death and may not be renewed; pending agreements of sale or lease may still proceed to consummation, but the appointed broker may not hire new licensees.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: When a broker of record for a partnership, association, or corporation dies, who must file an application designating a replacement, and within what deadline?
choice_a: A partner or corporate officer, within 15 days of the broker of record's death
choice_b: Any licensed salesperson employed by the entity, within 90 days
choice_c: The Commission itself appoints a replacement automatically, with no filing required
choice_d: The deceased broker of record's personal estate attorney, within 30 days
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.253 requires that, within 15 days following the death of a broker of record, a partner or corporate officer of the entity must file an application with the Commission designating another individual to serve as broker of record.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.254, within how many days must the Commission be notified that an interim broker or broker of record has been appointed when the original broker is unable to act due to illness or injury?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.254 requires the broker's attorney or power-of-attorney holder (for a sole proprietorship), or a corporate officer or partner, to notify the Commission within 15 days that another licensed broker has been appointed to act as interim broker or broker of record during the original broker's illness or injury.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.284, when must a licensee provide the written consumer disclosure summary if the initial interview with a consumer is NOT conducted in person?
choice_a: At the first subsequent in-person meeting with the consumer or when showing property, whichever occurs first
choice_b: Within 24 hours of the non-in-person initial interview, by certified mail
choice_c: Only at the signing of an agreement of sale, regardless of any earlier in-person contact
choice_d: The disclosure requirement is waived entirely whenever the initial interview is not in person
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.284 requires that when the initial interview with a consumer is conducted in person, the written disclosure summary must be provided at that meeting; when the initial interview is not in person, the licensee must instead provide it at the first subsequent in-person meeting or when showing property, whichever occurs first.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.284, which of the following is true regarding the consumer disclosure summary requirement?
choice_a: It does not apply to commercial property transactions involving non-individual consumers, and if a consumer refuses to sign the acknowledgment, that refusal must be documented
choice_b: It applies uniformly to every transaction with no exceptions, and a consumer's refusal to sign has no effect on the licensee's duties
choice_c: It applies only to residential sales, never to lease transactions of any kind
choice_d: A consumer's refusal to sign automatically voids the underlying transaction
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.284 exempts commercial property transactions involving non-individual consumers from the disclosure summary requirement, and requires a licensee to document it when a consumer declines to sign the acknowledgment of having received the disclosure.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: Under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(b), who may supervise the main or branch office of a CEMETERY broker, as distinct from the supervision rule for a standard real estate broker's office under subsection (a)?
choice_a: A broker, cemetery broker, associate broker, or associate cemetery broker holding a standard or reciprocal license
choice_b: Only a cemetery broker personally, with no substitute permitted under any circumstance
choice_c: Any salesperson designated in writing by the cemetery company
choice_d: A funeral director licensed by the State Board of Funeral Directors
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.244(b) broadens the pool of qualifying supervisors for a cemetery broker's office beyond subsection (a)'s broker/associate broker rule, permitting supervision by a broker, cemetery broker, associate broker, or associate cemetery broker holding a standard or reciprocal license.

topic: Broker Office Management, Branch Offices & Recordkeeping
question: What is the application fee for a branch office license under 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203's fee schedule?
explanation: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203's fee schedule lists $65 as the application fee for standard or reciprocal licensure of a branch office, distinct from the $75 fee for an initial broker/cemetery broker/rental listing referral agent license.
source_note: 49 Pa. Code Section 35.203 (confirmed via pacodeandbulletin.gov fee schedule)
